findings.title: Pillow BMP RLE delta escape amplifies ~1 KB uploads into ~1 GB RSS as the service account
findings.severity_rationale: Impact medium (availability of a shared service; bounds-safe decode, no code execution) x likelihood medium (unauthenticated local-network caller) gives low under the matrix. Counterexample: proof of internet exposure raises likelihood to high and the severity to medium.
findings.attacker: Local-network caller, no credentials (handle_upload has no auth). Lacks: any account, firewall bypass.
findings.sink: PIL BMP RLE decoder, pinned pillow==12.3.0 (CVE-2026-96638)
findings.dataflow: upload bytes -> size check -> Image.open().convert() -> PNG re-encode
findings.control: 100 MiB size cap (a size gate, not a content gate)
findings.impact: Per-request ~800,000x memory amplification as the service UID; concurrent uploads exhaust host RAM
findings.prerequisites: Crafted BI_RLE8 file (~1 KB); Pillow 12.3.0 as pinned
findings.counterevidence: No image-type or dimension gate precedes decode; the size cap does not bound decode memory.

codeEvidence.label: Raw upload bytes enter the handler
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker-chosen bytes arrive as body; nothing upstream inspects their format.

codeEvidence.label: Only a size cap guards decode
codeEvidence.code:
if len(body) > UPLOAD_LIMIT:
    raise ValueError("upload too large")
codeEvidence.explanation: The cap bounds input bytes, not decoded pixels, so a 1 KB RLE stream passes it.

codeEvidence.label: Pillow fully decodes attacker bytes
codeEvidence.explanation: convert() forces a full decode of the crafted BMP, where the delta-escape bug amplifies memory.

rootCause.summary: Upload bytes pass a size-only check and reach a full Pillow decode in the service process, where the pinned decoder's RLE delta escape turns a kilobyte into hundreds of megabytes.

validation.method: local PoC in the pinned interpreter (scratch dir, 4 GB address cap, 60 s timeout)
validation.summary: Crafted 1084-byte BI_RLE8 BMP per the advisory peaked at 878 MB RSS through the exact office.picture decode pattern.
assertions: Pinned Pillow 12.3.0 contains the RLE delta-escape amplification.
handle_upload decodes attacker bytes with the same call pattern as the PoC.
limitations: Peak measured on one host; other allocators may differ.

attackPath.summary: LAN caller posts a ~1 KB crafted BMP; the decode balloons service memory.

dataflow.outcome: hundreds of MB RSS per request

impact.why: Availability loss of a shared service; no code execution (bounds-safe sinks).

likelihood.why: Public advisory with exact reproduction; unauthenticated local-network trigger.

attackPath.crossBoundary: Verified to service-account RAM exhaustion; no privilege or data boundary crossed.
blindspots: Listener exposure beyond the local network (see coverage.unresolvable).

findings.remediation: Upgrade Pillow past the fixed release and bound decoded pixels (Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS, worker memory limits).
remediationTests: The 1084-byte PoC peaks under 50 MB RSS after the fix.
A 100 MB crafted BMP is rejected before full decode.
preventiveControls: Pin Pillow with OSV monitoring on every engine rebuild.
Gate all image decodes on dimensions before pixels.

non_findings.title: Oversized upload bypasses the 100 MiB cap
non_findings.reason: Control verified: the size check runs on the full body before decode on the only path.
